summary: A rapid response team holds an orientation for laid-off workers explaining services and benefits.
realLife: A federal page says specialists gather workers' skills and needs, then hold orientation meetings on career counseling, résumé and interview workshops, unemployment insurance, training and health and pension questions. Workers are urged to use services while severance or benefits last.
sources: U.S. Department of Labor, Rapid Response page for workers facing layoffs: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/layoffs/workers
inGame: Job-ended event followed by a notice of unemployment help; the game has no rapid-response record, so it needs: a local help office scene. Scene: needs a producer for layoff-terms.

turns.summary: The employer holds no orientation and the workers hear nothing about help.
turns.writesBack: Workers find services slowly, and the mood sours.

turns.summary: The workers are too shaken to attend and leave right away.
pulledBy: a layoff event announced in advance
turns.writesBack: Benefits start late and a journal note is made.

turns.summary: The orientation explains benefits clearly and workers sign up on the spot.
turns.writesBack: Benefits start sooner, ties among laid-off workers grow, and the mood eases.
